newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks near trading record on foreign buys.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks near trading record on foreign buys.

text.p: Mexican stocks extended their earlier advance to flirt with intraday records at midday dealing on Tuesday. Dealers said share prices gained on a continuing flow of foreign buying.
"The market is very solid, foreign money is still streaming in and there is no sign of any one jumping out. On the contrary, they like the market and think there's more to come," a floor trader said.
The leading IPC share index was up 37.80 points, or 0.74 percent, at 5,173.04, or just shy of a trading record of 5,178.54.

Athough less active than the frantic buying buying seen last week, dealers said trading volume of 84.6 million showed foreign fund flows were still strong enough to offset the adverse effect of forecast gains in primary interest rates.
Shares listed by financial group Bancomer accounted for most volume, and had gained strongly following news the firm had sold a portfolio of hotels for $133 million, dealers said.
Bancomer A shares were up 21 centavos to 3.63 pesos.
On the broad market, gainers outpaced decliners by 65 to 32, out of 117 stocks traded.
